source: Built-in ten-study effect/SE example; default options
plain: This analysis examined small-study effects in 10 studies. Egger’s test gave t = 5.047 and p < 0.001. Funnel asymmetry can have several explanations and does not establish publication bias. A lack of evidence of asymmetry does not establish its absence. The adjusted estimates are sensitivity analyses, not corrections known to remove bias.
methods: Effects and positive standard errors were analysed on the supplied scale, without transformation. Egger regressed the standardised effect on precision using unweighted least squares with multiplicative residual dispersion; the intercept used a two-sided t test with study count minus two degrees of freedom. Begg–Mazumdar correlated fixed-effect-centred, studentised effects with their variances using Kendall’s tau-b; its two-sided test uses the exact permutation distribution without ties and a tie-corrected normal approximation without continuity correction otherwise. The quantity labelled Thompson–Sharp on the page tests the intercept of the effect-on-SE regression (effect extrapolated to SE zero), not a test of asymmetry. It uses inverse-variance weights and multiplies its already dispersion-adjusted standard error by the square root of the larger of unity and residual dispersion, with a two-sided t test with study count minus two degrees of freedom. Trim-and-fill uses the L-zero estimator, chooses the filling side from the sign of a REML meta-regression slope on standard error, and uses REML for the trimmed and augmented fits; absolute residual ranks break ties by sorted order. The experimental Vevea–Hedges selection model uses maximum likelihood with Nelder–Mead optimisation and REML starting values, a one-sided normal p-value cutpoint of 0.025, and a chi-squared likelihood-ratio test against an unselected maximum-likelihood model with one degree of freedom. It is not validated against metafor. The page reports no confidence intervals, prediction intervals or heterogeneity summaries; none are inferred here. Analyses were run in allmeta pubbias-tests <build.version> (commit <build.shortSha>).
results: There were 10 studies. Egger: t = 5.047, p < 0.001; Begg–Mazumdar: tau-b = 0.796, p = 0.002. The effect-on-SE intercept (effect extrapolated to SE zero; labelled Thompson–Sharp on the page) is not a test of asymmetry: t = −0.501, p = 0.630. Trim-and-fill imputed 3 studies, with adjusted estimate 0.224. The experimental selection model gave relative selection weight δ₂ = 0.189, likelihood-ratio p = 0.097, adjusted mean 0.203 and unadjusted mean 0.247. All effects remain on the analysis scale. P-values below the reporting threshold are shown as bounds; other p-values retain the page’s rounding.
flags: Thompson–Sharp is outside the live R comparison. The selection model is experimental and not validated against metafor.
